claim: Interpretation: a CoWoS-class package is built in two stages—chip-on-wafer (dies and HBM bonded onto the interposer wafer) and on-substrate (the assembly attached to an organic substrate and tested). TSMC has historically done the CoW step and outsourced much of the oS step; OSATs are now moving into 'full process' (both steps), so the foundry-OSAT boundary sits inside one package.
notes: Based on ASE's distinction between 'OS type services and full process' (@c_ase_full, Q2 2026 call), the report that TSMC is outsourcing the CoW step (@c_cow_outs), UBS's 'Wafer-level Packaging (WoS) stage' remark (@c_ubs_osatshare) and CLM-1096.

claim: Inference: OSATs held roughly a quarter of CoWoS-class capacity at end-2026 on both public estimates found (UBS: ASE 20k + Amkor 20k of 160k; Economic Daily News: 50-60k of about 200k), so TSMC still held about three-quarters.
notes: Arithmetic from @c_ubs_ind26, @c_ubs_ase (40/160 = 25%) and CLM-1264 (50-60/~200 = 25-30%). Both are sell-side/press estimates with undisclosed definitions.
